title: Steve Farris v. Central Florida Presbytery
synopsis: The full Standing Judicial Commission found Steve Farris's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery judicially out of order because he was not a member of a PCA church and therefore lacked standing before the Commission.

title: Jeffrey M. Black v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
synopsis: TE Jeffrey Black complained that Eastern Carolina Presbytery failed to decide his complaint expressly and erred in ruling that a licentiate's view on the length of the creation days was not an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC held that the presbytery had effectively denied the complaint and did not err on the confessional question; a dissent was recorded.

title: Ed Fitzsimmons v. Evangel Presbytery
synopsis: The SJC found Ed Fitzsimmons's appeal against Evangel Presbytery administratively out of order because it was not filed with the Stated Clerk of the General Assembly within the thirty-day period required by BCO 42-2. The merits were not reached.

title: Smith v. Northeast Presbytery
synopsis: Frank J. Smith complained against Northeast Presbytery after Grace Presbyterian Church was dissolved and its members were placed under Presbytery's care. The SJC ruled the complaint in order, sustained it, and returned the matter to Presbytery for adjudication, holding that dissolution did not eliminate Presbytery's pastoral responsibility or Smith's standing in the pending case.

title: Roberts v. New River Presbytery
synopsis: Virgil B. Roberts complained that New River Presbytery delayed dissolving his pastoral relationship after he resigned and the congregation concurred. The SJC sustained the complaint, concluding that Presbytery should have acted on the agreed request rather than withholding dissolution; three commissioners dissented concerning Presbytery's constitutional authority and pastoral discretion.

title: Richard E. Olson, et al. v. Heritage Presbytery
synopsis: Richard E. Olson and others complained against Heritage Presbytery's response to a request for advice concerning officer abstinence from beverage alcohol. The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because it was untimely and held that a court's response to a non-judicial reference seeking advice is not a complainable action.

title: William A. Conrad, et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
synopsis: William A. Conrad and others complained that Central Carolina Presbytery failed to act when it sent their complaints to its commission serving as Prosperity Presbyterian Church's Interim Session. The SJC held that Presbytery had acted, found the complaint administratively out of order, and remanded the underlying complaints to the Interim Session as the court of original jurisdiction for timely adjudication.

title: Smith v. Northeast Presbytery
synopsis: Frank J. Smith challenged Northeast Presbytery's actions surrounding the dissolution of Grace Presbyterian Church and the administration of its former members. The SJC denied the complaint by a 20-2 vote, with a dissent disputing the majority's treatment of the complainant's constitutional and procedural claims.
description: Decision of the Standing Judicial Commission in Case 93-1, Frank J. Smith v. Northeast Presbytery, including the statement of facts, issues, judgment, reasoning, roll-call vote, and dissent.

title: Johnson v. Evangel Presbytery
synopsis: Edgar Davis Johnson appealed Evangel Presbytery's judgment in a disciplinary case arising from his pursuit of divorce on a claim of spiritual desertion. The SJC did not sustain the appeal, approving the proposed decision by a 21-1 vote.

description: Case 96-6 was dismissed as judicially out of order because the parties could not agree on the Record of the Case.

title: Adams v. Northeast Presbytery
vote: 17 concur; 1 concur in part and dissent in part; 5 absent
synopsis: TE Philip J. Adams complained about a Northeast Presbytery judicial matter while a related appeal was pending and sought a retrial of charges on which the accused had been acquitted. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order under BCO 43-1 and because the requested relief was unavailable. A separate opinion concurred in the result but dissented from part of the reasoning and urged clarification of appellate review after an acquittal.
description: Decision and separate opinion in Case 00-2, TE Philip J. Adams v. Northeast Presbytery, addressing complaints during an appeal and the scope of appellate review following acquittal.

title: Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery (Case 2002-02)

parties.complainant_or_appellant: RE Leland Nichols and RE Sam Couch

synopsis: Case 2002-02 was adjudicated with Cases 2001-34 and 2002-03 in the dispute over James River Presbytery's handling of the requested dissolution of a pastoral relationship. The SJC held that all complaints assigned to this docket were judicially out of order and addressed the related in-order complaints under the companion dockets in a consolidated judgment.

title: Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery (Case 2001-34)

parties.complainant_or_appellant: RE Leland Nichols and RE Sam Couch

synopsis: Case 2001-34 was decided with Cases 2002-02 and 2002-03. The SJC ruled one constituent complaint out of order, sustained the central challenge to James River Presbytery's delay in acting on a proper congregational request to dissolve a pastoral relationship, and denied the challenge to Presbytery's salary gift. The consolidated decision drew concurring and dissenting opinions.
description: Consolidated Standing Judicial Commission decision in Cases 2001-34, 2002-02, and 2002-03 concerning James River Presbytery's handling of a requested pastoral dissolution and related complaints.

The SJC answers the BCO 34-1 requests from Central Georgia, Southeast Alabama, and Savannah River Presbyteries (2020 Overtures 2, 4 and 25), by reference to the SJC's October 21, 2021, Decision in Case 2020-12: TE Ryan Speck v. Missouri Presbytery and the SJC’s March 3, 2022, Decision in Case 2020-05: TE Ryan Speck v. Missouri Presbytery. RE Mel Duncan requested that his negative vote be recorded.

title: Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery (Case 2002-03)

parties.complainant_or_appellant: RE Leland Nichols and RE Sam Couch

synopsis: Case 2002-03 was decided with Cases 2001-34 and 2002-02. The SJC ruled some constituent complaints out of order but sustained the central complaint that James River Presbytery unduly delayed acting on a congregation's proper request to dissolve its pastoral relationship; it denied a related complaint concerning a salary gift. The consolidated decision drew concurring and dissenting opinions.
description: Consolidated Standing Judicial Commission decision in Cases 2001-34, 2002-02, and 2002-03 concerning James River Presbytery's handling of a requested pastoral dissolution and related complaints.

title: Appeal of Jack Mayfield v. Siouxlands Presbytery
synopsis: Jack Mayfield appealed against Siouxlands Presbytery nearly a year and a half after the matter had been adjudicated. The General Assembly found the appeal not in order under BCO 42-4 because it was untimely and directed him to the procedure in BCO 37-4 for seeking removal of censure.
description: The published disposition of Appeal Case 4, item 13-61, in the report of the Committee on Judicial Business.

title: Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery
synopsis: The complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's debate and instruction that Christ Church, Oreland transfer three members. The commission did not sustain the debate specification but held that Presbytery lacked constitutional authority to command the transfers, sustained that specification, and annulled the instruction by an 18-0 vote.
description: Adjudication of Case #4 from the 16th General Assembly, adopted by the 17th General Assembly.

title: DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia Presbytery
synopsis: Complainants challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's disposition of indictments arising from the division of Christ Reformed Presbyterian Church, Oreland. The commission sustained the principal specifications, annulled Presbytery's adoption of its judicial commission report, tried the matters de novo, and imposed censures on ministers and former ruling elders.
description: Adjudication and trial record of Case #6 from the 16th General Assembly, adopted by the 17th General Assembly.

title: Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery
synopsis: The complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's reception of a complaint that had not first been filed with the primary court, its judgment of members without process, and its attempt to act for a Session. The commission sustained the errors, annulled the March 12, 1988 actions, and directed corrective action by an 18-0 vote.
description: Adjudication of Case #9 from the 16th General Assembly, adopted by the 17th General Assembly.

title: Sandra Lovelace v. Northeast Presbytery
synopsis: Sandra Lovelace submitted two letters challenging actions of Northeast Presbytery. The SJC found both administratively and judicially out of order because the first had not been presented first to the lower court and the second lacked supporting reasons and identified no complainable presbytery action under BCO 43-2 and 43-3.

title: Appeal of Randall Wright v. Northern California Presbytery
synopsis: Randall Wright appealed against Northern California Presbytery. The SJC found Case 2002-06 out of order, and the appeal was withdrawn before merits review.
description: Docket and final status in the 31st General Assembly SJC report.

title: Leland Nichols and Sam Couch v. James River Presbytery
synopsis: RE Leland Nichols and RE Sam Couch complained against James River Presbytery. The SJC found Case 2002-07 out of order and published no merits opinion under that docket number.
description: Docket and final status in the 31st General Assembly SJC report.

title: Westminster Presbyterian Church v. Westminster Presbytery
synopsis: Westminster Presbyterian Church complained against Westminster Presbytery, but withdrew Case 2004-01 before the SJC issued a merits decision.
description: Docket and withdrawn status in the 33rd General Assembly SJC report.

title: Appeal of Stuart Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
synopsis: TE Stuart Merriam appealed against Tennessee Valley Presbytery, but withdrew Case 2004-10 before the SJC issued a merits decision.
description: Docket and withdrawn status in the 33rd General Assembly SJC report.

title: David Kniseley et al. v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery
synopsis: TE David Kniseley and others challenged Rocky Mountain Presbytery's approval of the public title ‘Minister of Church Life’ for an unordained female staff member. The SJC denied the complaint, distinguishing the BCO's technical use of minister from generic staff titles and leaving the latter to lower-court judgment; a dissent disagreed.

title: Session of Crossroads Community Church v. Philadelphia Presbytery
synopsis: The Session of Crossroads Community Church challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensing and ordination of a candidate who stated a difference concerning women and the office of deacon but agreed to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery's judgment; a dissent argued it should have been sustained.

title: Mark Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
synopsis: RE Mark Grasso and others challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensure and ordination of Jason Hsu, who held a stated difference concerning women deacons but affirmed willingness to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery's actions; a dissent was recorded.

title: Appeal of TE Charles Tarter v. Evangel Presbytery
synopsis: TE Tarter appealed his deposition by Evangel Presbytery's Judicial Commission for failure to submit to presbytery authority. The SJC sustained multiple specifications of error—including that Presbytery's committee lacked authority to make certain demands, the indictment was inadequate, and hearsay evidence was improperly admitted—vacated the judgment and censure, and remanded the case for constitutionally compliant process or dismissal.

title: Stephen Hahn request concerning Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
synopsis: Stephen Hahn asked the SJC to assume original jurisdiction over Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery. The SJC found Case 2013-05 administratively out of order and did not reach the merits.
description: Docket and final status in the 42nd General Assembly SJC report.

title: Peter Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery (three complaints)
synopsis: Peter Benyola's three complaints against Central Florida Presbytery were found administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because he was no longer a member of a PCA congregation and therefore lacked standing. The SJC did not reach the merits.

title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
synopsis: TE Knox Baird and other elders challenged Grace Presbytery's handling of complaints, BCO 40-5 review requests, document demands, and a stay of pending trials arising from conflict at First Presbyterian Church of Hattiesburg. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main, rejected one specification, and did not reach another; concurring opinions were recorded.

title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
synopsis: Case 2023-08 was adjudicated with Case 2023-06 in the Baird complaints against Grace Presbytery. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main, rejected one specification, and did not reach another; concurring opinions were recorded.

title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
synopsis: RE Tom Turner challenged South Florida Presbytery's handling of matters involving Cross Community Church and the discipline of its pastor after the church voted to disaffiliate from the PCA. The SJC ruled the complaints administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing; two commissioners dissented.

title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
synopsis: Case 2023-17 was adjudicated with Case 2023-15. The SJC ruled Tom Turner's complaints administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing after Cross Community Church disaffiliated from the PCA; two commissioners dissented.

title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery

parties.complainant_or_appellant: TE Felipe Assis and TE Carter Brown

synopsis: TEs Felipe Assis and Carter Brown appealed South Florida Presbytery's decision to divest them without censure after their churches left the PCA. The SJC sustained the consolidated appeals, held that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 did not authorize divestiture on these facts, reversed the action, restored both ministers to good standing, and directed constitutionally appropriate further action.
description: Consolidated SJC decision in Appeals 2025-12 and 2025-13, dated December 15, 2025.

title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery

parties.complainant_or_appellant: TE Felipe Assis and TE Carter Brown

synopsis: Case 2025-13 was consolidated with Case 2025-12. The SJC sustained the appeals, reversed South Florida Presbytery's divestiture of TEs Felipe Assis and Carter Brown, restored them to good standing, and directed constitutionally appropriate further action.
description: Consolidated SJC decision in Appeals 2025-12 and 2025-13, dated December 15, 2025.
